```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(hydroloom)
eval <- (Sys.getenv("BUILD_VIGNETTES") == "TRUE") &
  requireNamespace("hydrogeofetch", quietly = TRUE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  eval = eval
)

library(sf)

oldoption <- options(scipen = 9999)
```

An index ties a point (a streamgage, a sample site, an intake) to a network.
`index_points_to_lines()` finds the flowline nearest each point and returns a
position on it: the flowline `id` and an `id_measure` along it. Where the
network carries an `aggregate_id` such as a reachcode, the index also carries
the `aggregate_id` and an `aggregate_id_measure` along the whole aggregate
flowpath. Both measures run from 0 at the outlet (downstream end) to 100 at the
inlet (upstream end).

The nearest flowline is often not the right one. A point near a confluence is
near two rivers, and a point on a lake shore is near a flowline that only
stands in for the lake. This article works through those cases with the
streamgages of the NHDPlusV2 sample in hydrogeofetch: indexing to vertices and
at higher precision, resolving ambiguity among nearby flowlines, locating an
index on its flowline, indexing to waterbodies, and measuring network distance
between two indexes. This article is website-only and does not run on CRAN.

# Flowlines

The sample covers part of the Yahara River basin above Lake Kegonsa. The gage
layer covers more than the flowlines do, so the comparisons below keep the
gages whose flowline (`FLComID`) is in the sample.

```{r data}
library(hydroloom)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

source(system.file("extdata/sample_data.R", package = "hydrogeofetch"))

flowlines <- sf::read_sf(sample_data, "NHDFlowline_Network") |>
  sf::st_zm()

gages <- sf::read_sf(sample_data, "Gage")
gages <- gages[gages$FLComID %in% flowlines$COMID, ]

nrow(flowlines)
nrow(gages)
```

`search_radius` is in the units of the points' projection, so both layers are
projected to Albers (meters) first. The search is a nearest neighbor search
against flowline vertices; see the [nn2 function from the RANN
package](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RANN) for how it works.

```{r index}
flowlines_5070 <- sf::st_transform(flowlines, 5070)
gages_5070 <- sf::st_transform(gages, 5070)

radius <- units::set_units(200, "m")

indexes <- index_points_to_lines(flowlines_5070, gages_5070,
  search_radius = radius)

head(indexes)
```

The output column names follow the input: `COMID` and `REACHCODE` stay as they
were, and the reachcode measure comes back as `REACHCODE_measure`. `point_id`
is the row of the point in `gages`.

The gage layer records the flowline and reachcode measure that NHDPlusV2
assigned each gage, so the index can be checked against it.

```{r compare}
compare <- function(indexes, gages) {
  i <- left_join(data.frame(point_id = seq_len(nrow(gages))),
    indexes[!duplicated(indexes$point_id), ], by = "point_id")

  same_reach <- !is.na(i$REACHCODE) & i$REACHCODE == gages$REACHCODE

  list(
    same_comid = sum(i$COMID == gages$FLComID, na.rm = TRUE),
    of = nrow(gages),
    measure_difference = round(quantile(
      i$REACHCODE_measure[same_reach] - gages$Measure[same_reach],
      probs = c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1)), digits = 2))
}

compare(indexes, gages)
```

26 of the 31 gages land on the same flowline, and the reachcode measures of
those on the same reachcode differ by up to about 20 (percent of the reachcode
length).

# Higher precision

Snapping to vertices limits a measure to the positions of the flowline
vertices. `precision` densifies the flowlines near
each point to the given spacing in meters (with `sf::st_segmentize()`) before
the search.

```{r precision}
indexes <- index_points_to_lines(flowlines_5070, gages_5070,
  search_radius = radius, precision = 10)

compare(indexes, gages)
```

All 31 gages now land on the gage layer's flowline and the measure differences
fall within 1. The flowline match improves along with the measure: with
vertices alone, the nearest vertex can belong to a neighboring flowline,
especially where two flowlines share an endpoint.

The gage geometry in the NHDPlusV2 gage layer has already been placed on the
flowlines, so this comparison shows that the index recovers NHDPlusV2's own
address for each gage. It says nothing about how far a gage's reported location
is from the network. The next section uses the reported locations.

# Resolving ambiguity

The gage layer carries each gage's reported longitude and latitude (`LonSite`,
`LatSite`). These sit off the network by up to a few hundred meters, and many
of them are within reach of more than one flowline. `max_matches` returns up to
that many candidate flowlines per point, nearest first.

```{r sites}
sites <- sf::st_drop_geometry(gages) |>
  filter(!is.na(LonSite)) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("LonSite", "LatSite"), crs = 4326)

sites_5070 <- sf::st_transform(sites, 5070)

candidates <- index_points_to_lines(flowlines_5070, sites_5070,
  search_radius = radius, precision = 10, max_matches = 10)

n_candidates <- table(candidates$point_id)
sum(n_candidates > 1)

compare(candidates, sites)
```

Taking the nearest candidate puts 22 of the 30 reported sites on the gage
layer's flowline. 12 sites have more than one candidate.

`disambiguate_indexes()` picks among the candidates for each point by comparing
an attribute of the flowline with an attribute of the point. Numeric attributes
pick the smallest difference. Character attributes pick the highest string
similarity (`utils::adist()`, ignoring case). The names of the two data frames
are not used; the first column of each joins to the index and the second holds
the attribute.

Drainage area is the usual numeric choice. The gage layer uses -999999 for a
missing drainage area, which has to be set to `NA` first; a point with no
drainage area drops out of the result.

```{r disambiguate}
gage_area <- sites$DASqKm
gage_area[gage_area < 0] <- NA

by_area <- disambiguate_indexes(candidates,
  sf::st_drop_geometry(flowlines[, c("COMID", "TotDASqKM")]),
  data.frame(point_id = seq_len(nrow(sites)), area = gage_area))

compare(by_area, sites)

by_name <- disambiguate_indexes(candidates,
  sf::st_drop_geometry(flowlines[, c("COMID", "GNIS_NAME")]),
  data.frame(point_id = seq_len(nrow(sites)), name = sites$STATION_NM))

compare(by_name, sites)
```

Both do worse against the gage layer than the nearest candidate: 15 of 30 by
drainage area and 19 by name. The table shows where they part ways.

```{r disambiguate-table}
multi <- as.integer(names(n_candidates[n_candidates > 1]))
fl_area <- function(id) round(flowlines$TotDASqKM[match(id, flowlines$COMID)], 1)

nearest <- candidates[!duplicated(candidates$point_id), ]

data.frame(
  station = substr(sites$STATION_NM[multi], 1, 32),
  gage_area = round(gage_area[multi], 1),
  gage_layer = fl_area(sites$FLComID[multi]),
  nearest = fl_area(nearest$COMID[match(multi, nearest$point_id)]),
  by_area = fl_area(by_area$COMID[match(multi, by_area$point_id)]))
```

The drainage areas are each flowline's total drainage area at its outlet. A
gage partway along a flowline drains less than that, and the gage's own
drainage area seldom agrees exactly with the network's. On the same river, the
flowline just upstream or downstream of the gage often comes closer in
drainage area than the flowline the gage is on (Lake Waubesa and Yahara River
at McFarland both pick the flowline with 847.9 km² over the one with 841.8
km²). Drainage area separates a large river from a small tributary well and
neighboring flowlines on one river poorly. Name has the opposite trouble: it
cannot separate flowlines on the same named river, and where a flowline has no
name it has nothing to compare.

The Yahara River at Windsor shows the case drainage area is good for.

```{r windsor}
windsor <- which(sites$SOURCE_FEA == "05427718")

windsor_candidates <- candidates[candidates$point_id == windsor, ]

left_join(windsor_candidates,
  sf::st_drop_geometry(flowlines[, c("COMID", "GNIS_NAME", "TotDASqKM", "Divergence")]),
  by = "COMID") |>
  select(COMID, GNIS_NAME, TotDASqKM, Divergence, offset)

by_area[by_area$point_id == windsor, ]
```

The gage reports 190.6 km². The nearest flowline, about 33 m from the reported
site, is an unnamed channel draining 63 km² that is coded as the minor path of
a divergence, and it is also the flowline the gage layer assigns. The Yahara
River flowline draining 191 km² is about 67 m away, and drainage area (and
name) pick it. For a question about what the gage drains, the Yahara River
flowline is the fit-for-purpose index even though it is neither the nearest
flowline nor the gage layer's.

```{r windsor-map, fig.height = 5}
windsor_site <- sites_5070[windsor, ]

plot(sf::st_geometry(sf::st_buffer(windsor_site, 300)), border = NA)
plot(sf::st_geometry(flowlines_5070), col = "grey70", add = TRUE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(flowlines_5070[flowlines_5070$COMID %in% windsor_candidates$COMID, ]),
  col = "grey30", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(flowlines_5070[flowlines_5070$COMID == sites$FLComID[windsor], ]),
  col = "orange", lwd = 3, add = TRUE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(flowlines_5070[flowlines_5070$COMID %in%
  by_area$COMID[by_area$point_id == windsor], ]), col = "blue", lwd = 3, add = TRUE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(windsor_site), pch = 16, add = TRUE)

legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
  legend = c("candidates", "gage layer flowline", "drainage area pick",
    "reported site"),
  col = c("grey30", "orange", "blue", "black"),
  lwd = c(2, 3, 3, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, NA, 16))
```

When the right flowline or reachcode is already known, there is nothing to
disambiguate. `ids` (one flowline id per point) and `aggregate_ids` (one
`aggregate_id` per point) constrain the search instead, so each point can only
land on its own flowline or on the flowlines of its own aggregate flowpath.
The constraint lets the search radius grow without pulling a point onto a
neighbor.

```{r constrain}
constrained <- index_points_to_lines(flowlines_5070, sites_5070,
  search_radius = units::set_units(500, "m"),
  aggregate_ids = sites$REACHCODE)

compare(constrained, sites)
```

28 of 30 sites land on the gage layer's flowline. The other two, on Lake
Kegonsa and Lake Monona, are more than 500 m from any flowline on their
reachcode and are not indexed; the waterbody section below returns to them.

# Locating an index

`get_hydro_location()` returns the point on the network for each index: the
hydro location the index refers to. It interpolates the `aggregate_id_measure`
along the flowline, so the flowlines need the reachcode from and to measures
(`FromMeas` and `ToMeas` in NHDPlusV2).

```{r hydro-location, fig.height = 5}
located <- get_hydro_location(constrained, flowlines)

plot(sf::st_geometry(flowlines), col = "grey60")
plot(sf::st_geometry(sites)[constrained$point_id], pch = 1, add = TRUE)
plot(located, pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = "blue", add = TRUE)

legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
  legend = c("reported site", "hydro location"),
  col = c("black", "blue"), pch = c(1, 16))
```

`offset` in the index is the distance from each point to its hydro location,
in the units of the points' projection (meters here).

```{r offset}
round(quantile(constrained$offset))
```

# Waterbodies

Seven of the gages are on lakes. For a point on a lake, the nearest flowline is
an artificial path through the lake, which stands in for the lake in the
network but is not the lake. `index_points_to_waterbodies()` finds the
waterbody each point is in or near, and with flowlines supplied, the flowline
at the waterbody's outlet (the lowest `Hydroseq` among the flowlines that carry
the waterbody's id).

```{r waterbodies}
waterbodies <- sf::read_sf(sample_data, "NHDWaterbody")

lakes <- grepl("LAKE", sites$STATION_NM)

on_lakes <- index_points_to_waterbodies(
  sf::st_transform(waterbodies, 5070),
  sites_5070[lakes, ],
  sf::st_drop_geometry(flowlines),
  search_radius = radius)

cbind(station = substr(sites$STATION_NM[lakes], 1, 32),
  on_lakes,
  gage_layer = sites$FLComID[lakes])
```

`in_wb_COMID` is set when a point falls inside a waterbody and `near_wb_COMID`
names the waterbody with the nearest shoreline within `search_radius`, at
`near_wb_dist` meters. For six of the seven lake gages, the outlet flowline
matches the gage layer's flowline, including Lake Monona, which the reachcode
constraint could not place. The Lake Kegonsa gage gets the outlet of the lake
while the gage layer puts it on another flowline.

Waterbody polygons must be single part. The NHDWaterbody layer stores
`MULTIPOLYGON` geometry with one part each, which is cast to `POLYGON`; a
waterbody with more than one part stops the function with an error.

# Network distance between indexes

The network distance between two indexes on the same flow path combines the
part of each flowline below its index with the length of the flowlines between
them. `get_partial_length()` returns the lengths below (`dn`) and above (`up`)
an index on its flowline. `navigate_connected_paths()` returns the distance
from the outlet of one flowline to the outlet of another, which needs the
network topology (`toid`) and `length_km`.

The Yahara River at Westport Road is above Lake Mendota and the Yahara River at
McFarland is below Lake Monona.

```{r distance}
westport <- constrained[constrained$point_id == which(sites$SOURCE_FEA == "05427851"), ]
mcfarland <- constrained[constrained$point_id == which(sites$SOURCE_FEA == "05429500"), ]

westport_partial <- get_partial_length(westport, flowlines)
mcfarland_partial <- get_partial_length(mcfarland, flowlines)

network <- add_toids(hy(sf::st_drop_geometry(flowlines)))

between <- navigate_connected_paths(network, c(westport$COMID, mcfarland$COMID))
between[, c("id_1", "id_2", "network_distance_km")]

westport_partial$dn + between$network_distance_km - mcfarland_partial$dn
```

The path runs from the outlet of the Westport Road flowline down to the outlet
of the McFarland flowline. Adding the part of the Westport Road flowline below
its index and removing the part of the McFarland flowline below its index
leaves the distance between the two gages along the network.

`get_subpath()` does this cut directly for two positions on one aggregate
flowpath and returns the pieces between them. Recording a position as a
distance from a confluence, placing it on another network, and cutting
subpaths are the subject of the [distances from confluences along mainstems
article](https://doi-usgs.github.io/hydroloom/articles/mainstem_referencing.html).
